title: the event log: every step of a run is a typed record
intent: The session log is append-only JSONL and it works, but its records have no vocabulary: there is no type for the start of a tool call, for the end of one, for a request of approval, for the refusal of one, for the spend of tokens. Both reference harnesses have a typed event union, and their interfaces render exactly that union. This wave gives the log that vocabulary, and the log becomes the event stream.
checks: ./scripts/dev ert tests/unit/test-yeah-state.el tests/unit/test-yeah-loop.el tests/unit/test-yeah-tools.el tests/unit/test-yeah-perm.el tests/unit/test-yeah-session.el tests/unit/test-yeah-compact.el tests/unit/test-yeah-undo.el tests/unit/test-yeah-acp.el tests/unit/test-yeah-emcp.el tests/unit/test-yeah-gptel.el tests/unit/test-yeah-subagent.el tests/unit/test-yeah-shell.el tests/unit/test-yeah-codes.el
objection: A vocabulary of events is a public contract, and a public contract in a project that has not shipped yet is a promise made twice: once in the schema and once in the code that writes it.
refuted_by: A client that renders the stream and a reader of the raw log that disagree about what a record means. If the schema and the writer can drift, the vocabulary is decoration.
